newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso frees students in peace gesture.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso frees students in peace gesture.

text.p: Burkina Faso's government has freed four detained student leaders and offered talks on their grievances once classes resume at the university.

The gesture, announced by state television late on Saturday by the minister of secondary and higher education and scientific research, followed a week of student unrest and boycotts that had spread to secondary schools.

"Once the situation returns to normal, the government is ready to open immediate discussions with the student representatives on their main concerns," the minister, Melegue Maurice Traore, announced on television.
He said the government had decided to free the student leaders following numerous calls from trades unions and society at large for action to defuse the crisis. The four were detained last Monday.
Traore said that the government was prepared to develop education, after taking account of the West African country's resources, but would crack down on violence from any quarter.
Police have used teargas to break up protests by students demanding the release of their leaders.

The National Association of Burkinabe Students (ANEB) called a strike from January 29 to back demands ranging from allowances for students not on formal grants to cheaper bus fares, improved food in the university restaurant and help with health expenses.
Burkina Faso's human rights watchdog MBDHP was among groups that urged dialogue to end the dispute.
